summary: The note is a Wikipedia article on the chronology of the Bible, describing the elaborate system of lifespans, generations and regnal synchronisms by which the Masoretic Hebrew Bible measures time from creation to about 164 BCE. It explains that this chronology is theological rather than historical, built around a schematic 4,000-year world cycle with the Exodus at its midpoint. The article also compares the Masoretic chronology with the Septuagint, Samaritan Pentateuch, Jubilees and Seder Olam, traces Christian dating traditions, and discusses the difficulty of reconciling the regnal chronology of the Israelite kings.
one_line: Overview of the schematic, theological timeline of the Masoretic Bible from creation to 164 BCE, and rival chronologies.
key_facts: The chronology of the Bible measures the passage of events from creation to around 164 BCE, the year of the re-dedication of the Second Temple.
The chronology is highly schematic, marking out a world cycle of 4,000 years.
The Exodus takes place in the year A.M. 2666, exactly two thirds of the way through the four thousand years.
The construction of Solomon's Temple is commenced 480 years, or 12 generations of 40 years each, after the Exodus.
430 years pass between the building of Solomon's Temple and its destruction during the siege of Jerusalem.
The Book of Jeremiah puts the Babylonian captivity at 70 years, while scholars established it lasted approximately fifty years.
The Book of Jubilees, dating from the 2nd century BCE, measures the interval from Creation to the settlement of Canaan as exactly fifty jubilees (2450 years).
Seder Olam Rabbah, dating from the 2nd century CE, allows 410 years for the First Temple and 420 years for the Second Temple.
Eusebius (c. 260–340) put the birth of Christ in AM 5199, which became the accepted date for the Western Church.
Venerable Bede calculated that Christ's birth took place in AM 3592.
Martin Luther placed the Apostolic Council of Acts 15 in the year AM 4000.
Archbishop James Ussher (1581–1656) calculated a date of 4004 BCE for creation, and his dates were incorporated into the margins of English Bibles for the next two hundred years.
Edwin R. Thiele's The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings (three editions between 1951 and 1983) is the most widely followed attempt to reconcile the contradictions in the Kings chronology.
The Books of Kings count 95 years passing in Judah and 98 in Israel for an interval that should have been equal.
The article describes the Masoretic chronology as perhaps embodying a 4,000-year scheme taking the re-dedication of the Temple by the Maccabees in 164 BCE as its end-point.

entities.name: Chronology of the Bible
entities.role: subject of the article, an elaborate system measuring time from creation in the Masoretic Hebrew Bible

entities.name: Masoretic Text
entities.role: Hebrew Bible text most commonly in use today, basis of modern Jewish and Christian bibles

entities.name: Septuagint
entities.role: Koine Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible whose chronology differs from the Masoretic Text

entities.name: Samaritan Pentateuch
entities.role: Samaritan version of the Torah whose chronology differs markedly from the Masoretic Text

entities.name: Book of Jubilees
entities.role: 2nd century BCE work measuring time in years, weeks of years and jubilees from Creation

entities.name: Seder Olam Rabbah
entities.role: 2nd century CE work tracing world and Jewish history from Creation

entities.name: James Ussher
entities.role: Archbishop of Armagh who calculated a date of 4004 BCE for creation

entities.name: Isaac Newton
entities.role: scholar who believed dating creation was knowable from the Bible

entities.name: Eusebius
entities.role: early church father who attempted to place Christ in the chronology

entities.name: Venerable Bede
entities.role: made his own calculations finding Christ's birth took place in AM 3592

entities.name: Martin Luther
entities.role: switched focus to the Apostolic Council of Acts 15, placed in AM 4000

entities.name: Edwin R. Thiele
entities.role: author of The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings, a widely followed attempt at reconciling the kings' chronology

entities.name: Alfred Jepsen
entities.role: proposed the Progenitor chronology based on the Samaritan and Masoretic recensions

entities.name: Jeremy Northcote
entities.role: scholar who discussed the Nehemiah chronology and the Proto-SP chronology

entities.name: Brevard Childs
entities.role: author of Introduction to the Old Testament as Scripture, which criticised Thiele's work

entities.name: Thomas L. Thompson
entities.role: author of The Mythic Past, source of the table summarising the Masoretic chronology

entities.name: Abraham
entities.role: patriarch whose birth is placed in AM 1948 in the Masoretic chronology

entities.name: Solomon
entities.role: king whose fourth regnal year marked the foundation of Solomon's Temple

entities.name: Cyrus the Great
entities.role: Persian ruler whose edict ended the Babylonian Exile and whose first regnal year is 538 BCE

entities.name: Paul the Apostle
entities.role: New Testament writer who agrees with the Septuagint and Samaritan Pentateuch on 430 years from Abraham to Moses

entities.name: Aaron
entities.role: first High Priest of Israel, representing the 26th generation from Adam

entities.name: Solomon's Temple
entities.role: temple whose foundation and destruction are central dates in the chronology

entities.name: Second Temple
entities.role: temple re-dedicated by the Maccabees in 164 BCE, the endpoint of the Masoretic 4,000-year cycle

entities.name: Maccabees
entities.role: group that re-dedicated the Second Temple in 164 BCE

entities.name: Exodus
entities.role: pivotal event of the chronology, placed in AM 2666

entities.name: Babylonian Exile
entities.role: period between the destruction of Solomon's Temple and Cyrus's edict, lasting 50 years in the chronology

entities.name: Kings of Judah
entities.role: related article on detailed reconstructions of the chronology of the Hebrew kings
